title: Ansel and the Alibi
premise: True-crime podcaster Ulyana Nystrom has spent seven years quietly documenting the unsolved disappearance of a local girl, keeping her own role as the case's only living witness buried in her alphabetized files. When a fresh body surfaces wearing clothes stolen from her closet, staged with details only she could know, Ulyana realizes the killer is someone who has studied her podcast as closely as she studied the case. Her investigation collides with Ansel Voss, the retired detective who once protected her identity and whom she never stopped loving, forcing her to choose between exposing her own secret testimony and letting him take the fall for murders he didn't commit. In the end, Ulyana baits the killer into confessing on-air using a fabricated detail from her closet, unmasking the town's beloved coroner, and chooses love over the anonymity that kept her alive.
about_author: Rafael Ashgrove is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent two decades transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. Ashgrove writes mysteries obsessed with what official records leave out, and lives near Lake Superior with an aging bloodhound named Verdict.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She records the final episode of her podcast season on the seven-year-old disappearance of Maren Kowalczyk, revealing to listeners everything except her own presence at the scene that night. A listener voicemail hints someone knows more than they should. Emotional beat: the false comfort of control through meticulous filing.

chapters.title: The Body Wore Her Clothes
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Sheriff's deputies pull a drowned woman from the reservoir dressed in Ulyana's stolen blouse and scarf, arranged exactly as described in episode twelve. Detective Ansel Voss, retired but consulting, arrives and their eyes meet across the tape line for the first time in seven years. Emotional beat: dread cracking open old longing.

chapters.title: Ansel's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. He rereads his old case ledger and admits to himself he falsified one entry to protect Ulyana's testimony back then, a choice that cost him his badge. Now the staging suggests the killer knows about that night. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into protective resolve.

chapters.title: Episode Thirteen
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She receives a letter quoting her unreleased draft notes verbatim, proving the killer has access to her home or her past. She audits her closet, her files, her memories, and finds a page torn from her original witness statement. Emotional beat: paranoia dissolving the walls between past and present.

chapters.title: What the Town Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Ulyana and Ansel uneasily pool information, retracing Maren's last night through the diner, the marina, and the coroner's office. Each interview reveals how many townspeople benefited from the case going cold. Emotional beat: the corrosive intimacy of shared secrets rekindling trust.

chapters.title: The Second Closet
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A second victim appears wearing clothes from Ansel's late wife's wardrobe, and the town whispers that the old detective has snapped. Ulyana alone recognizes the pattern: the killer is dressing victims as the people who failed Maren. Emotional beat: horror fused with fierce loyalty.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Arrested and questioned by his former protégé, now sheriff, Ansel refuses to reveal Ulyana's role even to save himself. Ulyana watches through the station glass, realizing her silence may cost him everything. Emotional beat: love against duty reaching its breaking point.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Reconstructing her missing statement page, she finally remembers the detail she suppressed for seven years: she saw the coroner's van at the marina that night and chose survival over truth. The killer isn't taunting her; he's recruiting her confession. Emotional beat: devastating self-recognition.

chapters.title: Live Broadcast
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Ulyana hijacks the airwaves with an emergency episode, seeding a fabricated detail about evidence hidden in her closet. The coroner, Dr. Pell, breaks into her home that night to destroy it while she records from the attic, Ansel arriving battered but armed with the sheriff. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into trap.

chapters.title: Off the Record
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. With Pell arrested on a recorded confession, Ulyana airs her true witness account, surrendering her invisibility and clearing Ansel of the falsified-entry scandal by testifying to why he did it. Weeks later, she and Ansel walk the reservoir shore together, the file finally closed. Emotional beat: grief, justice, and chosen love.
